DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.claim: Dhikr can mean verbal remembrance or mention.
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.anchor: الثاني : الذكر باللسان قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p160/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p160/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p160/r6.claim: Muslims should remember God; the Prophet’s advent is divine mercy that leads them from polytheism and disbelief into faith and religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p160/r6.anchor: The advent of the Prophet (sws) is a manifestation of the great mercy of God to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.claim: Against hypocrites' and mischief-makers' opposition, believers should disregard the uproar and increase remembrance and praise of God by night and day.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2.anchor: while disregarding their rumpus they should engage more and more in remembering God and in extolling Him by night and by day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.claim: God's remembrance is believers' shield against Satan; Qur'anic calls to persevere against enemies repeatedly direct believers to prayer, whose link to perseverance is discussed elsewhere in the tafsīr.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3.anchor: the real shield through which believers have to counter the onslaught of Satan and his progeny is God’s remembrance.

QASHANI:33:41-43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:33:41-43/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:33:41-43/r1.claim: Remembrance unfolds through the stations: spoken remembrance in the soul, presence in the heart, intimate conversation in the secret, witnessing in the spirit, union in the hidden, and annihilation in the Essence.
QASHANI:33:41-43/r1.anchor: باللسان في مقام النفس، والحضور في مقام القلب، والمناجاة في مقام السر

QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r4.claim: Love of God entails abundant remembrance, since people often mention what they love; heart remembrance can continue, while unceasing verbal remembrance is difficult.
QUSHAYRI:v3p40/r4.anchor: من أحب شيئا أكثر من ذكره ) فيجب أن تقول الله ، ثم لا تنس الله بعد ذكرك الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.claim: Another view says these formulas are the abundant remembrance, recited by the ritually pure, the sexually impure, and those in minor impurity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p360/r5.anchor: وقيل: المراد من قوله: "ذكرا كثيرا" هذه الكلمات يقولها الطاهر والجنب والمحدث

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r1.claim: The marriage to Zaynab showed that no man of the community would be a prophet whose son-wife would be forbidden, reinforcing Muhammad's finality.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r1.anchor: لأنه قضى أن لا نبوة بينه وبين أحد من رجال أمته توجب حرمة زوج الولد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r2.claim: Believers should remember God often by affirming His perfect attributes and praising Him, so they honor the Messenger, trust his complete truthfulness, and gain promised forgiveness and reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p114/r2.anchor: أي تصديقا لدعواكم ذلك { الله } الذي هو أعظم من كل شيء

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.claim: The author says other obligations have fixed limits and excuses, but remembrance has no endpoint and may be left only by someone overcome in reason.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r1.anchor: قوله {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا} يقول: لا يفرض على عبادة فريضة إلا جعل لها حدا معلوما ثم عذر أهلها في حال عذر

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.claim: The command to remember applies in every posture, time, place, circumstance, and condition; when people do so, God and His angels send blessings upon them.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r2.anchor: فقال: اذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم بالليل والنهار في البر والبحر في السفر والحضر في الغنى والفقر

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r3.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r3.claim: Maqatil says abundant remembrance includes praising, magnifying, declaring God’s oneness, and thanking Him with the tongue in every circumstance.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل في قوله {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا} قال: باللسان بالتسبيح والتكبير والتهليل والتحميد واذكروه على كل حال

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r5.claim: The Prophet says abundant remembrance outranks even a fighter who battles until his sword breaks and is stained with blood; Abu Saʿid transmits the report.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل أي العباد أفضل درجة عند الله يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r6.claim: The Prophet identifies the “solitary ones” as those who remember God abundantly; Abu Hurayra transmits the report.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سبق المفردون قالوا: وما المفردون يا رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v6p619/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r7.speaker: معاذ
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r7.claim: The Prophet says those who remember God most earn the greatest reward among the fighters, fasters, and performers of prayer, alms, pilgrimage, and charity; Abu Bakr remarks that they have taken all good, and the Prophet agrees.
DURR-FULL:v6p619/r7.anchor: عن معاذ رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن رجلا سأله فقال: أي المجاهدين أعظم أجرا قال: أكثرهم لله ذكرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r1.claim: God commands believers to remember Him abundantly because He has bestowed many kinds of blessings, bringing great reward and a good return.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى آمرا عباده المؤمنين بكثرة ذكرهم لربهم تعالى، المنعم عليهم بأنواع النعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r2.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet teaching that remembrance of God is the best and purest deed, raises ranks, and surpasses charity in gold and silver or fighting an enemy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r2.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r3.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi notes that some transmitters reported the Abu al-Darda hadith as mursal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r3.anchor: قال الترمذي: ورواه بعضهم عنه فأرسله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r4.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir notes a similar report through Mu'adh ibn Jabal from the Prophet, and says God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r4.anchor: أنه بلغه عن معاذ بن جبل، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، بنحوه، فالله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r5.claim: Abu Huraira says he keeps a prayer he heard from the Prophet: asking God to make him most grateful, most attentive to counsel, most given to remembrance, and most protective of the divine charge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: دعاء سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أدعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r6.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r6.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the Abu Huraira supplication report gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r6.anchor: ورواه الترمذي عن يحيى بن موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد المدني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r7.claim: Ahmad also transmits the same supplication from Abu Huraira through Abu Sa'id al-Madani.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r7.anchor: عن فرج بن فضالة، عن أبي سعيد المدني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r8.claim: The Prophet says the best person is one whose life is long and deeds good; when asked for a practice to hold fast to amid many Islamic duties, he says to keep the tongue moist with remembrance of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p431/r8.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن بسر يقول: جاء أعرابيان إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r1.claim: Tasbih means declaring God free of every unworthy attribute; subḥān min kadhā means how far removed He is from it.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r1.anchor: التسبيح: التنزيه، تقول: سبحان من كذا، أي: ما أبعده

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r2.claim: Al-Sabūḥ, with either an open or rounded initial vowel, names God as transcendent above what does not befit Him.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r2.anchor: وفي صفاته تعالى: السبوح بفتح السين وضمها، أي: المنزه عما لا يليق به

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r6.claim: Dhikran is an accusative cognate accusative, and kathīran modifies it.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r6.anchor: (ذكرا) نصب على المصدر، و(كثيرا) نعت له

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r11.claim: One proposed connection links the command to remember God with the preceding statement that Muhammad is God's Messenger, for which believers should give thanks.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r11.anchor: قيل: بقوله: (ولكن رسول الله) فمن عليهم به، فأمرهم أن يشكروه

JISHUMI:v8p5744/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r12.claim: Another proposed connection links the command to remember God with this statement and the blessings mentioned from the beginning of the sura.
JISHUMI:v8p5744/r12.anchor: وقيل: به وبما تقدم من النعم من أول السورة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r1.claim: Remember God by forms of praise such as sanctification, glorification, declaration of unity, and magnification, and do so abundantly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r1.anchor: أثنوا عليه بضروب الثناء من التقديس والتحميد والتهليل والتكبير وما هو أهله ، وأكثروا ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r3.claim: A prophetic report urges remembering God on every Muslim's tongue; another version says in every Muslim's heart.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 896 ) ( اذكروا الله على فم كل مسلم ) . وروي : ( في قلب كل مسلم ) .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r4.claim: Qatāda lists the formulas as Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu li-llāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, Allāhu akbar, and lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh al-ʿaliyy al-ʿaẓīm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r4.anchor: وعن قتادة : قولوا سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إلاه إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says these words may be said by a ritually pure person or by someone in a state of major ritual impurity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد : هذه كلمات يقولها الطاهر والجنب .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.claim: The commands to remember and glorify both apply to morning and evening, like saying 'fast and pray on Friday'; glorification is singled out from remembrance to mark its special merit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r6.anchor: والفعلان ، أعني اذكروا وسبحوا موجهان إلى البكرة والأصيل ، كقولك : صم وصل يوم الجمعة ، والتسبيح من جملة الذكر ، وإنما اختصه من بين أنواعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r7.claim: Glorification declares God's essence free of impermissible attributes and acts and absolves Him of repugnant things; its merit resembles the superiority of moral purity over other qualities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r7.anchor: لأن معناه تنزيه ذاته عما لا يجوز عليه من الصفات والأفعال ، وتبرئته من القبائح . ومثال فضله على غيره من الأذكار فضل وصف العبد بالنزاهة من أدناس المعاصي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.claim: Dhikr may mean increasing good works and worship, since every obedience and good deed is remembrance; morning-evening glorification may mean all prayers, which excel other acts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p554#2/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بالذكر وإكثاره : تكثير الطاعات ، والإقبال على العبادات ؛ فإن كل طاعة وكل خير من جملة الذكر ، ثم خص من ذلك التسبيح بكرة وأصيلا وهي الصلاة في جميع أوقاتها

MUQATIL:33:41-45/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:33:41-45/r1.claim: Believers are told to remember God frequently with their tongues.

TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says remembrance has no fixed limit or ordinary excuse for omission, unlike other duties; believers remember and glorify God in every condition, and God and the angels then pray for them.
TAB-FULL:v19p124/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا} [الأحزاب: 41] يقول: " لا يفرض على عباده فريضة إلا جعل لها حدا معلوما

TABATABAI:33:41-44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r2.claim: Dhikr is the opposite of forgetfulness: directing one's perception toward the thing remembered; speaking its names and attributes is only one instance of remembrance.
TABATABAI:33:41-44/r2.anchor: الذكر ما يقابل النسيان وهو توجيه الإدراك نحو المذكور وأما التلفظ بما يدل عليه من أسمائه وصفاته فهو بعض مصاديق الذكر.

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r1.claim: The Prophet calls abundant remembrance the best of deeds, highest in rank, purest with God, and better than wealth or fighting and dying in battle.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r1.anchor: ألا أخبركم بخير أعمالكم أرفعها في درجاتكم وأزكاها عند مليككم وخير لكم من الدينار والدرهم

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r2.claim: Asked who is best among the mosque's people, the Prophet answers: those who remember God most.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r2.anchor: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال من خير أهل المسجد؟ فقال أكثرهم لله ذكرا

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r3.claim: The person granted a remembering tongue has been granted the good of this world and the next.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r3.anchor: من أعطي لسانا ذاكرا فلقد أعطي خير الدنيا والآخرة

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r4.claim: An unattributed gloss of “do not give in order to receive more” says not to regard one's good work for God as abundant.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r4.anchor: لا تستكثر ما عملت من خير لله

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r5.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r5.claim: A report raised by Abū al-Muʿazzā says private remembrance counts as abundant remembrance, while hypocrites remember publicly but not privately, as in 4:142.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r5.anchor: وفيه بإسناده عن أبي المعزا رفعه قال قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام من ذكر الله في السر فقد ذكر الله كثيرا

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r6.claim: The author calls the inference from the hypocrites' public-only remembrance a subtle one.

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r7.claim: Through Zayd al-Shahhām, al-Ṣādiq names three especially severe tests for a believer: giving from one's wealth, fairness to oneself, and abundant remembrance of God.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r7.anchor: عن زيد الشحام قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام ما ابتلي المؤمن بشيء أشد عليه من ثلاث خصال يحرمها

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r8.claim: Abundant remembrance includes remembering God when facing what He permits and what He forbids, so that one obeys His limits.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r8.anchor: ولكن ذكر الله عند ما أحل له وذكر الله عندما حرم عليه.

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r9.claim: Remembering God is not limited to repeating phrases such as glorification, praise, the testimony of divine unity, and magnification, though those phrases are included.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r9.anchor: أما إني لا أقول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر وإن كان منه

TABATABAI:33:41-48/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r10.claim: In a report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī recorded by Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Bayhaqī, the Prophet says those who remember God much outrank even a warrior who fights until his sword breaks and is bloodied.
TABATABAI:33:41-48/r10.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سئل أي العباد أفضل درجة عند الله يوم القيامة؟

THALABI:v8p51/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p51/r1.speaker: محمد
THALABI:v8p51/r1.claim: The Prophet urges people to remember God often, even until they are called mad.
THALABI:v8p51/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أكثروا ذكر الله حتى يقولوا مجنون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r3.claim: Remembering God “much” means never forgetting Him in any circumstance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:33:39-43/r3.anchor: اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا } وهو أن لا ينسى على حال

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r1.claim: Remember God through what befits His majesty: declaring His oneness, praising, glorifying, and sanctifying Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r1.anchor: بما هو جل وعلا أهله من التهليل والتحميد والتمجيد والتقديس

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r2.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r2.claim: Several authorities understand much remembrance to mean remembering God during most times and circumstances.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r2.anchor: يعُم أغلب الأوقات والأحوال كما قال غير واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says much remembrance means never forgetting God; the same explanation is also reported from Mujāhid.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r3.anchor: وعن إبن عباس الذكر الكثير أن لا ينسى جل شأنه وروى ذلك عن مجاهد أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r4.claim: Another view is to remember God through His exalted attributes and beautiful names and to declare Him free of what is unbefitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r4.anchor: وقيل : أن يذكر سبحانه بصفاته العلى وأسمائه الحسنى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r5.claim: Muqātil defines it as saying the four formulas of glorification, praise, divine unity, and magnification in every circumstance.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r5.anchor: وعن مقاتل هو أن يقال : سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r6.speaker: العترة الطاهرة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r6.claim: The Prophet's family say that whoever says the four formulas thirty times has performed much remembrance of God.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r6.anchor: وعن العترة الطاهرة رضي الله تعالى عنهم من قال ذلك ثلاثين مرة فقد ذكر الله تعالى ذكرا كثيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r7.claim: Al-Majmaʿ cites al-Wāḥidī's chain from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim to Ibn ʿAbbās: Gabriel taught the Prophet an expanded remembrance formula, counted according to God's knowledge, weight, and fullness.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r7.anchor: عن الواحدي بسنده إلى الضحاك بن مزاحم عن إبن عباس قال : جاء جبريل عليه السلام إلى النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r8.claim: The cited report promises six merits: being recorded among frequent rememberers, precedence in day-and-night remembrance, a plant in Paradise, sins falling like leaves, God's gaze, and freedom from punishment for one God regards.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r8.anchor: فإنه من قالها كتب له بها ست خصال كتب من الذاكرين الله تعالى كثيرا وكان أفضل من ذكره بالليل والنهار

ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r9.claim: Some say that what counts as much is determined by customary usage.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says every obligation has a known limit and excuses for those in difficulty, but remembrance has no set limit and is excused only when reason is overcome.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يفرض الله تعالى فريضة (4) إلا جعل لها حدا معلوما، ثم عذر أهلها في حال العذر غير الذكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r2.claim: Remembrance is commanded in every condition, as also stated in 4:103: remember God standing, sitting, and lying on your sides.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r2.anchor: وأمرهم به في كل الأحوال، فقال: "فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم" (النساء-103)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r3.claim: Frequent remembrance means remembering God at night and day, on land and sea, in health and sickness, and in private and openly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r3.anchor: أي: بالليل والنهار، في البر والبحر وفي الصحة والسقم، وفي السر والعلانية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r4.claim: Mujahid says abundant remembrance means never forgetting God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p359/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الذكر الكثير أن لا تنساه أبدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:33:41/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:41/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:41/r1.claim: Remember God abundantly through most times and every kind of remembrance due Him: glorifying, praising, declaring oneness, and magnifying Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:33:41/r1.anchor: يغلب الأوقات ويعم الأنواع بما هو أهله من التقديس والتحميد والتهليل والتمجيد

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r1.claim: An opening report asks where the foremost devoted to God’s remembrance are and urges frequent remembrance as a way to graze in the gardens of Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r1.anchor: أين السابقون الذين يستهترون بذكر الله من أحب أن يرتع في رياض الجنة فليكثر ذكر الله

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r2.speaker: أم أنس
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r2.claim: Umm Anas reports the Prophet advising her to abandon sins as the best migration, keep the obligations as the best striving, and increase remembrance, the deed most beloved to God.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r2.anchor: عن أم أنس رضي الله عنها أنها قالت يا رسول الله أوصني قال: اهجري المعاصي فإنها أفضل الهجرة

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that whoever does not remember God abundantly has disavowed faith.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من لم يكثر ذكر الله فقد برىء من الايمان

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r4.claim: Abu Said al-Khudri reports the Prophet urging abundant remembrance until people call the worshipper mad.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أكثروا ذكر الله حتى يقولوا: مجنون

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet urging remembrance until hypocrites accuse the worshippers of showing off.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اذكروا الله حتى يقول المنافقون: انكم مراؤون

DURR-FULL:v6p620/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r6.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r6.claim: Abu al-Jawza reports the same prophetic exhortation: remember God abundantly, even if hypocrites call you show-offs.
DURR-FULL:v6p620/r6.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اكثروا من ذكر الله حتى يقول المنافقون: انكم مراؤون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.claim: Believers should replace arguing with or insulting hypocrites over rumors about the Prophet’s marriage to Zaynab with remembrance and praise, avoiding civic strife; this is more beneficial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4.anchor: أن يشغلوا ألسنتهم بذكر الله وتسبيحه ، أي أن يمسكوا عن مماراة المنافقين أو عن سبهم فيما يرجفون به في قضية تزوج زينب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.claim: The command resembles replacing tribal boasting with remembrance after pilgrimage, and avoiding speech that could provoke retaliation against God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5.anchor: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.claim: The instruction also follows the command to the Prophet to leave the hypocrites’ harm aside.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6.anchor: فهذا من نحو قوله لنبيئه { ودع أذاهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.claim: If believers continue that dispute after this command, their conduct marks them as hypocrites, since believers obey their Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7.anchor: وفيه تسجيل على المنافقين بأن خوضهم في ذلك بعد هذه الآية علامة على النفاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.claim: The passage opens a new address but remains connected to what precedes through contextual relevance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8.anchor: والجملة استئناف ابتدائي متصل بما قبله للمناسبة التي أشرنا إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r9.claim: Dhikr here means remembrance by the tongue, which best fits the surrounding verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r9.anchor: والذكر : ذكر اللسان وهو المناسب لموقع الآية بما قبلها وبعدها .

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r1.claim: The preceding practical advice says fullness causes illness; if eating is necessary before cupping, first taste a little.
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r1.anchor: وعلى الشبع داء إلا إذا كان به ضرر فليذق أولا شيئا قليلا ثم ليحتجم

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r2.claim: The cited regimen advises avoiding intercourse for a day and a night before and after cupping, and avoiding a bath on the day of cupping or bloodletting.
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r2.anchor: وإذا أراد الحجامة يستحب أن لا يقرب النساء قبل ذلك بيوم وليلة وبعده مثل ذلك ولا يدخل في يومه الحمام

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r3.claim: Bustan al-ʿĀrifīn advises avoiding salty foods, meat from the head, and dairy after cupping; vinegar, broth, and sweets are recommended.
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r3.anchor: ولا يأكل رأسا ولا لبنا ولا شيئا مما يتخذ من اللبن

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r4.claim: The author closes the medical advice by invoking God as healer and sufficiency.

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r5.claim: Remembering God includes saying what befits Him, such as the declarations of divine oneness, praise, and greatness.
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r5.anchor: بما هو أهله من التهليل والتحميد والتكبير ونحوها

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r6.claim: Dhikr is bringing something to mind in the heart or in speech; remembrance after forgetting is the state of ordinary people, while sustained presence and mindfulness is the elite’s state.
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r6.anchor: والذكر إحضار الشيء في القلب أو في القول وهو ذكر عن نسيان وهو حال العامة أو إذامة الحضور والحفظ وهو حال الخاصة

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r7.claim: Remember God continually in every time, place, and condition; in obedience seek sincerity and acceptance, in sin abstain and repent, in blessings give thanks, and in hardship be patient. Dhikr has no fixed limit or excuse except loss of reason.
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r7.anchor: في جميع الأوقات ليلا ونهارا صيفا وشتاء وفي عموم الأمكنة برا وبحرا سهلا وجبلا وفي كل الأحوال حضرا وسفرا صحة وسقما

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r8.claim: The states of people who remember God vary according to their forms of remembrance.

BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r9.claim: A lower form of remembrance stays on the tongue, without thought, heart-presence, spiritual intimacy, witnessing divine lights, or inward self-annihilation.
BURSEVI:v7p147#2/r9.anchor: فذكر بعضهم بمجرد اللسان بدون فكر مذكوره ومطالعه آثاره بعقله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r1.claim: Mujāhid explains abundant remembrance as never forgetting God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد هو أن لا ينساه أبدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib explains abundant remembrance as the five daily prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r2.anchor: وقال ابن السائب يقال ذكرا كثيرا بالصلوات الخمس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r3.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān takes it as glorification, praise, profession of unity, and magnification in every circumstance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان هو التسبيح والتحميد والتهليل والتكبير على كل حال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet quoted God as saying He is with His servant whenever the servant remembers Him and moves his lips for Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p396/r4.anchor: وقد روى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال يقول ربكم أنا مع عبدي ما ذكرني وتحركت بي شفتاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r1.claim: The Prophet urges people to remember God abundantly, even until observers call them mad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أكثروا ذكر الله حتى يقولوا: مجنون."

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas has the Prophet urge abundant remembrance until hypocrites accuse the rememberers of showing off.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r3.claim: The Prophet says a gathering that contains no remembrance of God will be a source of regret on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما من قوم جلسوا مجلسا لم يذكروا الله فيه، إلا رأوه حسرة يوم القيامة."

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says remembrance has no fixed limit and no excuse for leaving it except being overcome and unable; other obligations have defined limits and excuses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r4.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: {اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir applies the command across night and day, land and sea, travel and residence, wealth and poverty, health and illness, privacy and publicity, linking it to 4:103.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r7.claim: The verse strongly urges abundant remembrance of God; Ibn Kathir notes that many verses, reports, and traditions encourage it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p432/r7.anchor: وفي هذه الآية الكريمة الحث على الإكثار

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r1.claim: The passage presents God as remembering people despite being independent of them, while they need Him; they should remember His favors, including His blessing them through prayer.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r1.anchor: الغني عنكم يذكركم، وأنتم المحتاجون إليه فاذكروه، وقيل: عد نعمه، ومن ذلك صلاته عليهم

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r2.claim: One view takes frequent remembrance as remembrance by the tongue, invoking God’s beautiful names and exalted attributes; another locates it in the heart.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r2.anchor: قيل: هو باللسان بذكر أسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العلا، وقيل: بالقلب

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God set a limit for every obligation except remembrance, which has no limit and is commanded in every circumstance.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: لم يفرض الله على عباده فريضة إلا جعل لها حدا غير الذكر، فإنه لم يجعل له حدا

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r4.claim: One account defines abundant remembrance as belief in divine oneness and justice, obligatory in all states except forgetfulness and sleep.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r4.anchor: قيل: هو اعتقاد التوحيد والعدل وأنه واجب في جميع الأحوال لا يجوز تركه بحال إلا حال النسيان والنوم

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r5.claim: Another account means verbal remembrance in all circumstances, places, and times, privately and publicly.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو ذكر الله باللسان في عموم الأحوال والأمكنة والأزمنة في السر والعلانية

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r6.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses abundant remembrance as not forgetting God.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r6.anchor: وقيل: الذكر الكثير: ألا تنساه، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r7.claim: Another explanation is to remain obedient to God always and never disobey Him.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو أن تكون على طاعته أبدا لا تعصيه

JISHUMI:v8p5745/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r8.claim: Remembrance may also mean turning to God with hope and fear and seeking His protection.
JISHUMI:v8p5745/r8.anchor: وقيل: اذكروه بالرغبة إليه والرهبة منه والاعتصام به

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r1.claim: One interpretation is continual remembrance in the heart that leads to obedience and avoidance of disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r1.anchor: أحدهما : ذاكروه بالقلب ذكرا مستديما يؤدي إلى طاعته واجتناب معصيته

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r2.claim: Al-Suddi interprets it as abundant remembrance with the tongue.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r2.anchor: الثاني : اذكروا الله باللسان ذكرا كثيرا , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet urged abundant remembrance for anyone unable to keep vigil at night, too cowardly to fight, or too stingy to spend wealth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( من عجز عن الليل أن يكابده , وجبن عن العدو

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr says remembrance here is supplication and entreaty to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r4.anchor: قاله ابن جبير . الثاني : الإقرار له

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r5.claim: Another explanation is affirming God’s lordship and acknowledging one’s servitude to Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p409/r5.anchor: الثاني : الإقرار له بالربوبية والاعتراف له بالعبودية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#2/r1.claim: Remember God through varied forms of praise and do so abundantly.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p308#2/r1.anchor: أثنوا عليه بضروب الثناء وأكثروا ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r1.claim: God commands His servants to remember and thank Him abundantly; the command has no fixed limit because it is easy and its reward is great.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى عباده بأن يذكروه ويشكروه

QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one is excused for neglecting remembrance of God except someone whose reason has been overcome.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يعذر أحد في ترك ذكر الله

QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد والنبي
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r3.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the Prophet urged people to remember God until others would call them mad.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r3.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أكثروا ذكر الله

QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r4.claim: One view calls remembrance abundant when sincere from the heart, and scant when it is merely hypocritical speech on the tongue.
QURTUBI-FULL:33:41/r4.anchor: وقيل: الذكر الكثير ما جرى على الإخلاص من القلب

RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r1.claim: The sura’s theme is disciplining the Prophet: it first treats his duty toward God and his family, then commands believers as God commands His messengers, beginning with reverence for Him.
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r1.anchor: وجه تعلق الآية بما قبلها هو أن السورة أصلها ومبناها على تأديب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r2.claim: Believers may forget God, so they are commanded to remember Him continually; the Prophet does not forget, but is commanded to fear God because closeness can lessen fear and even the elect remain at risk.
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r2.anchor: المؤمن قد ينسى ذكر الله فأمر بدوام الذكر ، أما النبي لكونه من المقربين لا ينسى ولكن قد يغتر المقرب من الملك بقربه منه فيقل خوفه

RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r3.claim: The description “much” is apt because, as al-Razi has explained elsewhere, there is no impediment to remembering God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p185#3/r3.anchor: قد ذكرنا أن الله في كثير من المواضع لما ذكر وصفه بالكثرة إذ لا مانع من الذكر

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r1.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r1.claim: The command means one should never forget God, at any moment.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r1.anchor: one to not forget God ever, at any moment (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r2.claim: The Prophet counseled a man to keep his tongue always moist with God's remembrance.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r2.anchor: when the Prophet counseled a man, “Let thy tongue be always moist with the remembrance of God,”

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r3.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet urged remembrance until people call one mad.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r3.anchor: he is reported to have said, “Remember God much, till they call [you] mad” (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r4.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says duties have known limits and excuses except remembrance, which has no limits or excuse unless someone is oppressed and forced to neglect it.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r4.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said, “God did not enjoin any duty upon His servants without setting known limits

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r5.claim: Frequent remembrance is said to arise from sincerity of heart, while little remembrance is likened to hypocritical remembrance on the tongue alone.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r5.anchor: remembering God frequently arises from the sincerity of the heart, while remembering God little arises from hypocrisy

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r6.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAjībah says the verse means remembrance of the heart, which alone does not cease.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r6.anchor: what is meant by this verse is remembrance of the heart, as that is the one type of remembrance that does not cease

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r7.claim: Dhikr is considered the quintessential prayer and the core of every act of worship.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r7.anchor: considered the quintessential prayer and thus to be at the core of every act of worship

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r8.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r8.claim: A report says those who remember God most have the greatest reward among strivers, the righteous, and worshippers in prayer, alms, pilgrimage, and charity; Abū Bakr tells ʿUmar they acquired every good, and the Prophet agrees.

STUDYQURAN:33:41/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r9.claim: Further discussion of God's remembrance appears at 13:28 and 29:45c.
STUDYQURAN:33:41/r9.anchor: For more on the remembrance of God, see 13:28c; 29:45c

SULAMI:v2p148#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p148#4/r1.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p148#4/r1.claim: While other acts of worship have appointed times, remembrance is commanded abundantly: the heart should not lapse from witnessing or become heedless of the Divine Presence.
SULAMI:v2p148#4/r1.anchor: قال النصرآباذي : وقت الله العبادات بأوقات إلا الذكر فإنه أمر أن يذكر كثيرا

TABRISI:33:41/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:41/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:33:41/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās transmits from the Prophet: whoever cannot endure the night, fight the enemy, or spend wealth should increase remembrance of God.
TABRISI:33:41/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

TABRISI:33:41/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:41/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:33:41/r2.claim: Mujāhid says abundant remembrance means never forgetting God.
TABRISI:33:41/r2.anchor: هو أن لا ينساه أبدا عن مجاهد

TABRISI:33:41/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:41/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:33:41/r3.claim: Another view says to remember God by His exalted attributes and beautiful names and declare Him free of what is unfitting.
TABRISI:33:41/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو أن يذكره سبحانه بصفاته العلى

TABRISI:33:41/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:41/r4.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:33:41/r4.claim: Maqātil says abundant remembrance is saying the four phrases of glorification, praise, unity, and greatness in every circumstance.

TABRISI:33:41/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:41/r5.speaker: أئمتنا
TABRISI:33:41/r5.claim: The Imams say reciting these phrases thirty times counts as abundant remembrance.
TABRISI:33:41/r5.anchor: وقد ورد عن أئمتنا ع أنهم قالوا:

TABRISI:33:41/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:41/r6.speaker: زرارة وحمران عن أبي عبد الله
TABRISI:33:41/r6.claim: Zurāra and Ḥumrān ibn Aʿyan transmit from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that the Tasbīḥ of Fāṭima al-Zahrāʾ counts as abundant remembrance.
TABRISI:33:41/r6.anchor: وعن زرارة وحمران ابني أعين عن أبي عبد الله ع قال:

TABRISI:33:41/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:33:41/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:33:41/r7.claim: Al-Wāḥidī transmits via al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās that Gabriel taught a quantified formula of remembrance, promising six merits: abundant remembrance, superiority to ordinary night-and-day remembrance, a tree in Paradise, falling sins, God’s regard, and protection from punishment.
TABRISI:33:41/r7.anchor: روى الواحدي بإسناده عن الضحاك بن مزاحم عن ابن عباس قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī takes abundant remembrance to mean remembrance with the tongue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: ذكرا كثيرا باللسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r2.claim: Muqātil also takes abundant remembrance to mean remembrance with the tongue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: ذكرا كثيرا باللسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains it as never forgetting God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو ألا ينساه أبدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī also explains abundant remembrance as the five daily prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ويعني ذكرا كثيرا بالصلوات الخمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r5.speaker: ابن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ḥayyān says it is glorifying, praising, declaring God’s oneness and greatness in every situation, with the formulas subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu li-llāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, and Allāhu akbar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن حيان: هو التسبيح والتحميد والتهليل والتكبير على كل حال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r6.claim: A report received by the author says that a person in major ritual impurity, after relieving himself, or in a state of minor impurity may say these remembrance formulas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p262#2/r6.anchor: وبلغنا أن هؤلاء الكلمات يتكلم بهن صاحب الجنابة والغائط والحدث

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r5.claim: Al-Suddi explains abundant remembrance of God as remembrance with the tongue.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r6.claim: This remembrance has no fixed time and is voluntary.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r6.anchor: وهذا ذكر ليس فيه وقت وهو تطوع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda calls remembrance the best deed, purifying with God and better than giving gold and silver or fighting and being killed in battle.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء، قال: ألا أخبركم بخير أعمالكم، أزكاها عند مليككم،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r8.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r8.claim: Abu Bahriyya reports Muadh ibn Jabal’s saying that no human deed saves more from God’s punishment than abundant remembrance of God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r8.anchor: فقال أبو بحرية: قد قال ذاك أخوكم معاذ بن جبل: ما عمل آدمي قط عملا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r9.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that people who gather solely to remember God are called from heaven to rise forgiven, with their sins changed into good deeds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p723/r9.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما من قوم اجتمعوا يذكرون الله

ELMALILI:33:41-42/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r1.claim: Frequent remembrance covers all times and all forms of fitting remembrance, including sanctifying, magnifying, declaring God’s oneness, and praising Him.
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r1.anchor: çok zikir vakitlere gālib ve takdis, temcid, tehlil, tahmid gibi Allah’a lâyık zikrin envâ‘ına şâmil olur.

ELMALILI:33:41-42/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:33:41-42/r4.claim: Both remembrance and tasbih also include prayer.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.claim: Believers are first urged to remember God frequently without limiting the subject or form, then directed toward glorification, probably referring to the prayers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1.anchor: Öncelikle “anma”nın konusu ve şekli sınırlanmadan çok olması teşvik edilmiş, sonra, muhtemelen namazlar kastedilerek tenzih şeklindeki anmaya yönlendirme yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.claim: Remembering God with tongue and heart, reflecting on Him, and keeping Him in awareness form the indispensable energy and lifeline of servitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2.anchor: Allah’ı dil ve gönülle anmak, O’nu düşünmek ve bilincinde tutmak kulluğun vazgeçilmez enerjisini, hayat damarını teşkil etmektedir

BURHAN:v2p137/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p137/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p137/r5.claim: Repeating the testimony about the Messenger accords with God being a sufficient witness; repetition more strongly fulfills the call’s purpose of public announcement and signals abundance.
BURHAN:v2p137/r5.anchor: وتكرار الشهادة للرسول في معنى قوله وكفى بالله شهيدا

BURHAN:v2p400/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p400/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p400/r6.claim: Scholars differ on whether a cognate accusative or the verb is preferable for emphasis: the noun is lighter, while the verb can suggest continuity.
BURHAN:v2p400/r6.anchor: هل الاولى التاكيد بالمصدر أو الفعل قال بعضهم المصدر اولى

BURHAN:v2p400/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p400/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p400/r7.claim: A cognate accusative naming an action's kind normally takes a descriptive adjective; an adjective can also be supplied by an annexed phrase.
BURHAN:v2p400/r7.anchor: حيث اكد المصدر النوعي فالاصل فيه ان ينعت بالوصف المراد منه

ITQAN:v3p178/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p178/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p178/r4.claim: The usual emphatic accusative is qualified by an adjective, as in remembering God much and releasing women graciously.
ITQAN:v3p178/r4.anchor: والأصل في هذا النوع أن ينعت بالوصف المراد نحو

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.claim: Reports from Mu'adh ibn Anas, Ibn Mardawayh, and Jabir say that whoever says Subhan Allah al-Azim receives a planted tree or palm tree in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r1.anchor: عن معاذ بن أنس رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من قال سبحان الله العظيم نبت له غرس في الجنة

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.claim: The Prophet urges saying Subhan Allah wa bi-hamdihi and describes these as two near or readily accessible words, as the excerpt phrases it.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم يقول سبحان الله وبحمده انهما القريبتان

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever says Subhan Allah wa bi-hamdihi a hundred times in a day has sins erased, even if they are like the foam of the sea.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من قال في يوم مائة مرة سبحان الله وبحمده

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.speaker: عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.claim: Abdullah advises a woman from Hamdan, who counted glorifications with pebbles or seeds, to say Allahu akbar kabiran wa subhanallahi bukratan wa asila instead.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r4.anchor: عن هلال بن يسار رضي الله عنه قال: كانت امرأة من همدان تسبح وتحصيه بالحصى أو النوى فقال لها عبد الله

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.claim: The Prophet asks whether anyone can earn a thousand good deeds in a day and answers that a hundred glorifications earn a thousand good deeds and erase a thousand sins.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r5.anchor: عن سعد رضي الله عنه قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لنا يعجز أحدكم أن يكسب في اليوم ألف حسنة

DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.speaker: سليم بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.claim: A man tells Abu Umama that he dreamed angels prayed for him whenever he entered, left, stood, or sat; Abu Umama says they may have angels pray for them too if they remember and glorify God, citing 33:41–42.
DURR-FULL:v6p621/r7.anchor: عن سليم بن عامر رضي الله عنه قال: جاء رجل إلى أبي أمامة فقال: إني رأيت في منامي أن الملائكة تصلي عليك
